summary: I sent the scripted prompt once. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the source, the tests and src/ui/, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (406 lines). The plan's page code builds the page from the component library: pageHeader, filterBar, selectField, dataTable, statusChip and emptyState. The plan says outright that it does not copy services.js. The agent asked no clarifying questions and changed no source, test, data or public file in the working tree.
reasoning: All four criteria are met, based on the session log, the plan file on disk and a clean git status. The plan builds the table and the environment filter with the library's dataTable and selectField instead of copying the hand-written Services page.

observations.description: Without being prompted, the agent tested the plan's code in a throwaway copy of the repo built with git archive in a temp dir. This caught a wrong assumption in one of its server tests (search also deploys to production), and it fixed the plan. That is useful, but it is real execution during a planning-only request. It ran outside the working tree, so it did not break the 'don't implement' rule. Still, some users may not expect it.

The agent says the extra Codex review of the plan was skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed, and that the skip was 'recorded in the ledger'. A user is unlikely to know what that ledger is or where it lives. The append ran through the plugin's ungated-ledger script, and I found no new file in the working tree.

The plan lists the choices it made where the spec is silent ('All environments' sends env=, default sort direction, chip tones, raw timestamp, empty-state wording) and asks the reader to check them. That is helpful.
When Claude Code starts, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit', so a stray Enter quits the session. This is upstream behaviour and not something this test covers.
docs/ is gitignored in the fixture (`!! docs/`), so the plan file is untracked and will not be committed by default. This may be intended.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log is {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` printed 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gave 406 lines. The agent's closing summary describes the plan as written and asks me to read it.

criteria.criterion: Page code calls the library's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table> or <select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's code for src/pages/deploys.js starts with `import { dataTable, emptyState, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js';` and calls `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` inside filterBar, and `dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort, sortHref, empty: emptyState(...) })`. grep finds `<table` and `<select` only in test assertions (lines 139 and 170) and in an implementer note. They do not appear in the page code.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source, test, data or public file changed)
criteria.evidence: Afterwards, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` printed nothing and `git diff --stat HEAD` was empty. `git status --ignored` listed only `!! docs/`. The session log shows the only Write/Edit calls were on docs/hyperpowers/plans/... . The agent ran its trial of the code in a mktemp copy built with `git archive HEAD` under /var/folders/..., not in the working tree.
